417	title: Filters
418	description: Stack up to four filters on a clip, from Blur and Pixelate to Sepia and Vignette, set how strong each one is, and animate them.
419	---
420	
421	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
422	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
423	
424	Filters change how a clip looks: soften it, break it into blocks, turn it black and white, darken its corners. A clip can carry up to four at once, and any clip that draws can have them, text, shapes and graphics included.
425	
426	<AtAGlance
427	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Filters"
428	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end', 'paste_attributes']}
429	/>
430	
431	## Add a filter
432	
433	<Steps>
434	
435	1. Select the clip and open the **Clip** tab's [**Picture**](/canvas/picture-tab/) sub-tab.
436	
437	2. Open the **Filters** section. On a clip with none it reads "No filters on this clip."
438	
439	3. Choose **Add Filter**. A Blur at 50 % joins the end of the stack.
440	
441	4. Pick the filter you want in the row's popup that reads **Blur**, and set its **Amount**.
442	
443	</Steps>
444	
445	Changing a filter's kind keeps its **Amount**. A clip can hold four, as the "4 at most" beside **Add Filter** says, and the button greys out at that point.
446	
447	Each change is one undo step. While the section is closed, its header shows `none`, the filter's name, or a count such as `3 filters`.
448	
449	## The seven filters
450	
451	| Filter | What it does | At 100 % |
452	| --- | --- | --- |
453	| **Blur** | Softens the picture. | A radius of 24 pixels |
454	| **Sharpen** | Crisps up edges and fine detail with an unsharp mask. | A gain of 2 |
455	| **Pixelate** | Breaks the picture into square blocks. The clip's edge and rounded corners stay clean. | Blocks 64 pixels across |
456	| **Sepia** | Gives the picture a warm old-photo tone. | The full tone |
457	| **Noir** | Turns the picture black and white and adds contrast. Taking **Saturation** to its lowest only removes the colour. | Fully black and white |
458	| **Vignette** | Darkens towards the edges in an ellipse fitted to the clip's cropped shape. The darkening starts a little under halfway from the centre to the corners. | Black corners |
459	| **Invert** | Turns the picture into its negative. | The full negative |
460	
461	Blur and Pixelate are measured in the clip's own pixels. Scale a clip up and the effect grows with it, and the same **Amount** looks finer on a 4K clip than on a 1080p one.
462	
463	## Set how strong a filter is
464	
465	**Amount** runs from 0 to 100 %, with quick picks at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100. At 0 the filter stays on the clip and does nothing. Sepia, Noir and Invert mix from the original picture towards their full effect as the number rises.
466	
467	## Stack and reorder filters
468	
469	Each filter's row starts with a number popup, which is its place in the stack. Pick a different number to move the filter. You can't drag rows. A move is one undo step.
470	
471	The place doesn't decide everything, because Frame Job always works through a stack in this order:
472	
473	1. Pixelate, whatever its place.
474	2. The **Color** section of the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/): **Brightness**, **Contrast**, **Saturation** and **Hue**.
475	3. Blur and Sharpen, whatever their places.
476	4. The rest of the Color tab: **Light**, **Wheels**, **Curves** and **Look**.
477	5. Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert, in the order of their places.
478	
479	So the order only changes the picture among Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert. Noir then Sepia gives a warm black and white, while Sepia then Noir gives a plain one. Moving a Blur above or below a Sepia changes nothing.
480	
481	Filters of the same kind combine:
482	
483	| In one stack | You get |
484	| --- | --- |
485	| Two Blurs | One wider blur. Two at 100 % reach a radius of about 34 pixels, and four reach 48. |
486	| Two Sharpens | The sum of the two. |
487	| Two Pixelates | The coarser of the two. |
488	
489	## Remove a filter
490	
491	Choose **Remove** in the filter's row. **Reset** in the section's header takes off the whole stack, and it's there only while no action is selected.
492	
493	## Animate a filter
494	
495	An [action](/motion/actions/) can ramp a filter's **Amount**, for example a blur that builds across a clip.
496	
497	<Steps>
498	
499	1. Add the filter and set **Amount** to where the ramp should start.
500	
501	2. Add an action on the clip and keep it selected.
502	
503	3. Set **Amount** to where the ramp should end.
504	
505	</Steps>
506	
507	With an action selected, each control does something different:
508	
509	| You change | What happens |
510	| --- | --- |
511	| **Amount** | It ramps across the action. |
512	| The filter's kind | It switches at the action's end, and the row shows "at end". The other filters keep ramping. |
513	| The filter's place | It moves at the action's end. |
514	| **Add Filter** or **Remove** | It changes the clip itself rather than the action, so it isn't animated. |
515	
516	:::caution
517	Adding or removing a filter while an action already animates the stack leaves the two stacks different lengths. The action stops ramping them and the filters switch at its end instead. To get the ramp back, select the action, choose **Clear** in the section's header, then set the clip's amounts and the action's again.
518	:::
519	
520	See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for how the rows behave in an action.
521	
522	## Filters on an adjustment clip
523	
524	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) has no **Picture** sub-tab, so it can't take a filter from the inspector. It gets one through [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) instead.
525	
526	<Steps>
527	
528	1. Put Sepia, Noir, Vignette or Invert on an ordinary clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
529	
530	2. Select the adjustment clip.
531	
532	3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.
533	
534	</Steps>
535	
536	The filter then applies to everything behind the adjustment clip for as long as it lasts, and to nothing on a track in front.
537	
538	Blur, Sharpen and Pixelate can't go on an adjustment clip, because it has no picture of its own to sample. Pasting from a clip that has one stops with an error naming the clip and the filter, and changes nothing.
539	
540	:::caution
541	Paste Attributes replaces the target's picture settings, not only its filters. Pasting onto an adjustment clip overwrites its grade and its Strength with the copied clip's, so paste first and grade afterwards.
542	:::
543	
544	## Good to know
545	
546	- A filter covers the whole picture for the whole clip. To blur or pixelate one region, such as a face, use [Obscure](/effects/obscure/).
547	- With several clips selected, the rows show the first clip's stack, and any edit gives every selected clip that whole stack.
548	- A [nest](/editing/nests/) clip shows the Filters section, but a filter on it has no effect. Put filters on the clips inside the nest.
549	- On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), a clip's filters shape the cut it makes. **Alpha** and **Inverted Alpha** read only transparency, so Sharpen, Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert change nothing there.
550	- A clip's [reflection](/effects/reflection/) shows its filters too.
551	
552	## With an agent
553	
554	An agent sets a clip's filters with `set_video`, as a list of kinds and amounts, with each amount from 0 to 1. The list replaces the old one whole, so it sends every filter it wants to keep, and an empty list clears the stack. A fifth filter is an error, and nothing changes. It can put Sepia, Noir, Vignette or Invert straight onto an adjustment clip, with no paste. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#filters).
555	
556	With `set_action_end`, an agent can give an action a list of a different length, which switches at the action's end rather than ramping. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end).
557	
558	## Related
559	
560	- [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)

563	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)
564	- [The Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/)
565	- [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/)
